114: 
115: ## CID
116: ```
117: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
118: │                          How CID Works                                       │
119: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
120: │                                                                             │
121: │  1. User creates event record                                               │
122: │     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐                                     │
123: │     │ {                               │                                     │
124: │     │   "$type": "ngo.islamu.event...",│                                    │
125: │     │   "title": "Community Iftar",   │                                     │
126: │     │   "startsAt": "2025-03-15...",  │                                     │
127: │     │   ...                           │                                     │
128: │     │ }                               │                                     │
129: │     └─────────────────────────────────┘                                     │
130: │                    │                                                        │
131: │                    ▼                                                        │
132: │  2. PDS serializes to DAG-CBOR (deterministic binary format)               │
133: │                    │                                                        │
134: │                    ▼                                                        │
135: │  3. PDS computes SHA-256 hash → CID                                        │
136: │     ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
137: │     │ bafyreigxyz123... (base32 encoded multihash)                │        │
138: │     └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
139: │                    │                                                        │
140: │  4. CID is included in the repo commit (signed by user's key)              │
141: │                                                                             │
142: │  WHY THIS MATTERS:                                                          │
143: │  ─────────────────                                                          │
144: │  • Anyone can verify the record hasn't been tampered with                  │
145: │  • If content changes → CID changes → old references become invalid        │
146: │  • Enables "strong references" (URI + CID = exact version)                 │
147: │                                                                             │
148: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
149: ```
150: 
151: ## Identity System Hybrid Approach (Planned)
152: 
153: > **⚠️ Planned Feature**: The hybrid authentication system is not yet implemented.
154: > **Current State**: Only Keycloak/OIDC authentication is active. ATProto OAuth integration is planned.
155: 
156: **Planned Approach**: Support BOTH Keycloak (traditional) AND ATProto OAuth, with custodial DIDs for Keycloak users:
157: 
158: ```
159: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
160: │                    Hybrid Auth Architecture                                  │
161: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
162: │                                                                             │
163: │                      ┌─────────────────┐                                    │
164: │                      │   Login Page    │                                    │
165: │                      └────────┬────────┘                                    │
166: │                               │                                             │
167: │              ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐                            │
168: │              ▼                                 ▼                            │
169: │    ┌──────────────────┐              ┌──────────────────┐                  │
170: │    │ Login with Email │              │ Login with ATProto│                  │
171: │    │   (Keycloak)     │              │ (Bring your DID)  │                  │
172: │    └────────┬─────────┘              └────────┬─────────┘                  │
173: │             │                                  │                            │
174: │             ▼                                  ▼                            │
175: │    ┌──────────────────┐              ┌──────────────────┐                  │
176: │    │ Keycloak returns │              │ ATProto OAuth    │                  │
177: │    │ UUID + email     │              │ returns DID      │                  │
178: │    └────────┬─────────┘              └────────┬─────────┘                  │
179: │             │                                  │                            │
180: │             ▼                                  ▼                            │
181: │    ┌──────────────────┐              ┌──────────────────┐                  │
182: │    │ Create custodial │              │ Link existing    │                  │
183: │    │ DID for user     │              │ DID to account   │                  │
184: │    └────────┬─────────┘              └────────┬─────────┘                  │
185: │             │                                  │                            │
186: │             └────────────────┬─────────────────┘                            │
187: │                              ▼                                              │
188: │                    ┌──────────────────┐                                     │
189: │                    │  user + actor    │                                     │
190: │                    │  records created │                                     │
191: │                    └──────────────────┘                                     │
192: │                                                                             │
193: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
194: ```
195: 
196: ## Handling Nullable DID (did_status)
197: 
198: The key insight is that DID creation is **async**. Here's how to handle it:
199: ```
200: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
201: │                    DID Status State Machine                                  │
202: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
203: │                                                                             │
204: │  ┌─────────┐     Background job      ┌─────────┐                           │
205: │  │ pending │ ──────────────────────▶ │ active  │                           │
206: │  └─────────┘     creates DID         └─────────┘                           │
207: │       │                                                                     │
208: │       │ DID creation fails                                                  │
209: │       ▼                                                                     │
210: │  ┌─────────┐     Retry succeeds      ┌─────────┐                           │
211: │  │ failed  │ ──────────────────────▶ │ active  │                           │
212: │  └─────────┘                         └─────────┘                           │
213: │                                                                             │
214: │  WHAT USERS CAN DO:                                                         │
215: │  ──────────────────                                                         │
216: │  pending → Browse, edit profile (read-heavy)                                │
217: │  failed  → Same as pending, show "retry" button                            │
218: │  active  → Full access: post events, comment, etc. (write access)          │
219: │                                                                             │
220: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
221: ```
````

## File: docs/MODULAR_EVENTS.md
````markdown
  1: # Modular Event Architecture
  2: 
  3: > **Cultural and Domain-Specific Event Customization**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes how the platform supports deep customization for different
  6: > cultural, religious, and domain-specific event types through the aspect pattern.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: Events are the core aggregate of the platform. Rather than using inheritance to handle different event types (Islamic, Tech, Educational, etc.), the platform uses a **composition-based aspect pattern** that allows:
 15: 
 16: - Any event to have multiple "aspects" simultaneously
 17: - Cultural customization without schema changes
 18: - Domain-specific fields added per tenant
 19: - Graceful degradation when aspects are unavailable
 20: 
 21: ---
 22: 
 23: ## The Aspect Pattern for Events
 24: 
 25: ### Core Event vs Aspects
 26: 
 27: | Component | Contains | Example |
 28: |-----------|----------|---------|
 29: | **Core Event** | Universal properties | Title, date, organization, status |
 30: | **Islamic Aspect** | Religious customization | Madhab, prayer time offset, gender segregation |
 31: | **Tech Aspect** | Technical events | GitHub repo, hackathon track |
 32: | **Educational Aspect** | Learning events | Certification, prerequisites |
 33: 
 34: ### Why Not Inheritance?
 35: 
 36: | Scenario | Inheritance Approach | Aspect Approach |
 37: |----------|---------------------|-----------------|
 38: | Islamic Conference | `IslamicEvent` class | Event + Islamic aspect |
 39: | Tech Hackathon | `TechEvent` class | Event + Tech aspect |
 40: | Islamic Tech Conference | `IslamicTechEvent` class? | Event + Islamic aspect + Tech aspect |
 41: | 5 event types | 31 possible classes | 5 aspect tables |
 42: 
 43: **Aspect pattern scales linearly; inheritance scales exponentially.**
 44: 
 45: ---
 46: 
 47: ## Islamic Event Customization
 48: 
 49: ### Islamic-Specific Attributes
 50: 
 51: | Attribute | Purpose | Values |
 52: |-----------|---------|--------|
 53: | **Madhab** | Jurisprudence school | Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali, Mixed |
 54: | **Prayer Time Offset** | Schedule relative to prayer | Minutes before/after Fajr, Dhuhr, etc. |
 55: | **Gender Segregation** | Attendance policy | Men-only, Women-only, Segregated, Mixed |
 56: | **Language Mode** | Primary language | Arabic, English, Urdu, etc. |
 57: 
 58: ### Prayer-Based Scheduling
 59: 
 60: Instead of absolute times, events can be scheduled relative to prayer times:
 61: 
 62: | Scheduling Mode | Description |
 63: |-----------------|-------------|
 64: | **Absolute** | Standard datetime (default) |
 65: | **After Prayer** | X minutes after specified prayer |
 66: | **Before Prayer** | X minutes before specified prayer |
 67: | **Between Prayers** | Between two specified prayers |
 68: 
 69: **Benefit**: Same event "30 minutes after Maghrib" automatically adjusts for different locations and dates.
 70: 
 71: ### Gender Segregation Modes
 72: 
 73: | Mode | Description | Facility Requirements |
 74: |------|-------------|----------------------|
 75: | **Men Only** | Restricted to men | Single section |
 76: | **Women Only** | Restricted to women | Single section |
 77: | **Segregated** | Both attend, separate areas | Dual sections, barriers |
 78: | **Family** | Families together, singles separate | Family + singles sections |
 79: | **Mixed** | No segregation | Open seating |
 80: 
 81: ---
 82: 
 83: ## Tech Event Customization
 84: 
 85: ### Tech-Specific Attributes
 86: 
 87: | Attribute | Purpose | Example |
 88: |-----------|---------|---------|
 89: | **Repository URL** | Code repository link | GitHub, GitLab URL |
 90: | **Hackathon Track** | Competition category | AI, Web, Mobile |
 91: | **Skill Level** | Required expertise | Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced |
 92: | **Stack Tags** | Technologies used | .NET, React, Python |
 93: 
 94: ---
 95: 
 96: ## Event Type Resolution
 97: 
 98: ### Determining Active Aspects
 99: 
100: When loading an event:
101: 
102: 1. **Core data** always loaded
103: 2. **Aspect presence** determined by existence of aspect record
104: 3. **UI components** rendered based on present aspects
105: 4. **Validation** applies aspect-specific rules
106: 
107: ### API Response Structure
108: 
109: Events include metadata about active aspects:
110: 
111: | Field | Purpose |
112: |-------|---------|
113: | `id`, `title`, etc. | Core event data |
114: | `aspects[]` | List of active aspect identifiers |
115: | `islamicDetails` | Islamic aspect data (if present) |
116: | `techDetails` | Tech aspect data (if present) |
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: ## Module-Based Aspect Availability
121: 
122: ### Tenant Configuration
123: 
124: Tenants enable aspects through module configuration:
125: 
126: | Tenant Type | Enabled Modules | Available Aspects |
127: |-------------|-----------------|-------------------|
128: | Mosque | Core, Islamic | Basic + Islamic |
129: | Tech Community | Core, Tech | Basic + Tech |
130: | University | Core, Islamic, Educational | Basic + Islamic + Educational |
131: 
132: ### Aspect Visibility
133: 
134: Aspects appear in UI only when:
135: 1. ✅ Module enabled at instance level
136: 2. ✅ Module activated for tenant
137: 3. ✅ User has permission to use it
138: 
139: **Result**: A tech community never sees "Madhab" dropdown; a mosque never sees "GitHub Repo" field.
140: 
141: ---
142: 
143: ## Creating Events with Aspects
144: 
145: ### Event Creation Flow
146: 
147: 1. **Select Intent** → "What type of event?" (filters by tenant's modules)
148: 2. **Core Details** → Title, description, organization
149: 3. **Aspect Details** → Dynamic forms based on selected aspects
150: 4. **Review & Publish** → Validation across all aspects
151: 
152: ### Dynamic Form Generation
153: 
154: The API returns form schema based on active aspects:
155: 
156: | Request | Response |
157: |---------|----------|
158: | `GET /api/events/schema` | Core fields only |
159: | `GET /api/events/schema?aspects=islamic` | Core + Islamic fields |
160: | `GET /api/events/schema?aspects=islamic,tech` | Core + Islamic + Tech fields |
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## Validation Across Aspects
165: 
166: ### Aspect-Specific Validation
167: 
168: Each aspect can contribute validation rules:
169: 
170: | Aspect | Validation Rule | Example |
171: |--------|-----------------|---------|
172: | Islamic | Prayer time must be valid | Can't schedule during Jumah prayer |
173: | Tech | Repository URL must be accessible | GitHub URL returns 200 |
174: | Educational | Prerequisites must exist | Referenced courses must exist |
175: 
176: ### Cross-Aspect Validation
177: 
178: Some validations span multiple aspects:
179: 
180: | Rule | Aspects Involved |
181: |------|------------------|
182: | "Women-only tech workshop" | Islamic (gender) + Tech (track) |
183: | "Prayer break during hackathon" | Islamic (prayer) + Tech (hackathon) |
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## Querying Events by Aspect
188: 
189: ### Filtered Queries
190: 
191: Events can be queried by aspect presence:
192: 
193: | Query | Returns |
194: |-------|---------|
195: | All events | Events regardless of aspects |
196: | Islamic events | Events with Islamic aspect |
197: | Tech events | Events with Tech aspect |
198: | Islamic tech events | Events with both aspects |
199: 
200: ### Aspect-Specific Filters
201: 
202: Within an aspect, specific filters apply:
203: 
204: | Filter | Aspect | Example |
205: |--------|--------|---------|
206: | By Madhab | Islamic | "Hanafi events only" |
207: | By Gender | Islamic | "Women-only events" |
208: | By Track | Tech | "AI hackathon events" |
209: | By Stack | Tech | ".NET events" |
210: 
211: ---
212: 
213: ## Extending with New Aspects
214: 
215: ### Adding a New Aspect
216: 
217: To add a new event aspect (e.g., "Medical"):
218: 
219: 1. **Define Aspect Table** → `EventMedicalDetails` with medical-specific fields
220: 2. **Create Module** → Package aspect with logic and UI
221: 3. **Register** → Add to module catalog
222: 4. **Enable** → Instance/tenant can activate
223: 
224: ### Aspect Independence
225: 
226: Aspects should be:
227: - **Self-contained** → No dependencies on other aspects
228: - **Gracefully optional** → Events work without any aspects
229: - **Backward compatible** → New aspects don't break existing events
230: 
231: ---
232: 
233: ## Related Documentation
234: 
235: - **[EXTENSIBILITY.md](EXTENSIBILITY.md)** - General aspect architecture
236: - **[MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md)** - Tenant module configuration
237: - **[DOMAIN.md](DOMAIN.md)** - Entity relationships
238: 
239: ## Implementation Reference
240: 
241: For code patterns:
242: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** skill - Optional 1:1 relationships
243: - **`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`** skill - Handler patterns for aspects
````

## File: docs/MULTI_TENANCY.md
````markdown
  1: # Multi-Tenancy Architecture
  2: 
  3: > **Conceptual Guide for Multi-Tenant System Design**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes the multi-tenancy model, authority hierarchy, and data isolation patterns.
  6: > For implementation details and code patterns, see the relevant skills in `.claude/skills/`.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform operates as a **multi-tenant system** where multiple independent organizations (tenants) share the same application infrastructure while maintaining complete data isolation. The architecture supports both dedicated single-tenant deployments and shared multi-tenant SaaS models.
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Hierarchy of Authority
 19: 
 20: ### Two-Tier Administration Model
 21: 
 22: The system distinguishes between two fundamentally different administrative roles:
 23: 
 24: | Tier | Role | Scope | Typical Use Case |
 25: |------|------|-------|------------------|
 26: | **Tier 1** | Instance Administrator | Infrastructure, global policies, module enablement | SaaS provider, IT department |
 27: | **Tier 2** | Tenant Administrator | Community data, local configuration, user management | Organization leader, community admin |
 28: 
 29: ### Instance Administrator (Super Admin)
 30: 
 31: **Responsibilities:**
 32: - Physical server and infrastructure management
 33: - Global resource limits and quotas
 34: - Module enablement/disablement at platform level
 35: - Enforcement policies that cannot be overridden
 36: - Tenant provisioning and lifecycle management
 37: - System-wide security policies
 38: 
 39: **Cannot Do:**
 40: - Access tenant-specific business data
 41: - Make decisions on behalf of tenants
 42: - Override tenant preferences within allowed bounds
 43: 
 44: ### Tenant Administrator (Customer)
 45: 
 46: **Responsibilities:**
 47: - Community-specific configuration
 48: - User management within their tenant
 49: - Branding and customization
 50: - Local business rules and workflows
 51: - Content moderation policies
 52: 
 53: **Constrained By:**
 54: - Instance-level enforcement policies
 55: - Module availability set by Instance Admin
 56: - Resource quotas and limits
 57: 
 58: ---
 59: 
 60: ## Cascading Configuration Engine
 61: 
 62: ### Resolution Strategy
 63: 
 64: Settings are resolved at runtime using a **fall-through strategy**:
 65: 
 66: 1. **Check Tenant Override** → Does the tenant have a specific value?
 67: 2. **Check Instance Enforcement** → Is this setting locked by the Instance Admin?
 68: 3. **Fall to Default** → Use the system default value
 69: 
 70: ### Setting Types
 71: 
 72: | Type | Behavior | Example |
 73: |------|----------|---------|
 74: | **Locked** | Tenant cannot override | Security policies, payment provider |
 75: | **Delegated** | Tenant may customize | Theme colors, notification preferences |
 76: | **Default-Only** | System default, no UI exposed | Internal technical settings |
 77: 
 78: ### Enforcement Scenarios
 79: 
 80: **Scenario: Render Mode Control**
 81: - Instance Admin sets `RenderMode = Auto` with `IsLocked = false`
 82: - Tenant Admin sees a dropdown and can change to `Server` or `WebAssembly`
 83: - If Instance Admin sets `IsLocked = true`, dropdown is disabled/hidden
 84: 
 85: **Scenario: Module Restriction**
 86: - Instance Admin configures `AllowedModules = ["Core", "Islamic"]`
 87: - Tenant Admin cannot enable "Tech" module even if code exists
 88: - Tenant only sees modules within their allowed set
 89: 
 90: ---
 91: 
 92: ## Data Isolation
 93: 
 94: ### Tenant Boundary Enforcement
 95: 
 96: Every tenant-scoped entity implements `ITenantEntity`:
 97: - Contains `TenantId` property
 98: - Automatically filtered in all queries via global query filters
 99: - Cannot be accidentally accessed across tenant boundaries
100: 
101: ### Isolation Guarantees
102: 
103: | Layer | Mechanism |
104: |-------|-----------|
105: | **Database** | Global query filters on `TenantId` |
106: | **Application** | Tenant context injected per-request |
107: | **API** | Middleware validates tenant claims |
108: | **UI** | Routes scoped to tenant context |
109: 
110: ### Cross-Tenant Operations
111: 
112: Cross-tenant operations are **explicitly forbidden** except:
113: - Instance Admin reporting and analytics
114: - System-wide notifications (opt-in)
115: - Federation sync (ATProto/ActivityPub)
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Tenant Lifecycle
120: 
121: ### Provisioning Flow
122: 
123: 1. **Request** → Tenant Admin requests new tenant (or Instance Admin creates)
124: 2. **Validation** → Check quotas, naming conflicts, policy compliance
125: 3. **Creation** → Database schema initialized with tenant seed data
126: 4. **Configuration** → Module selection, initial settings
127: 5. **Activation** → Tenant becomes operational
128: 
129: ### Tenant States
130: 
131: | State | Description | Operations Allowed |
132: |-------|-------------|-------------------|
133: | **Pending** | Created but not activated | Configuration only |
134: | **Active** | Fully operational | All operations |
135: | **Suspended** | Temporarily disabled | Read-only access |
136: | **Archived** | Soft-deleted | None (data retained) |
137: | **Purged** | Permanently deleted | None (data removed) |
138: 
139: ---
140: 
141: ## Single-Tenant vs Multi-Tenant Deployment
142: 
143: ### Virtual Tenant Strategy
144: 
145: The codebase is **always multi-tenant internally** to avoid maintaining separate codebases. Single-tenant mode is achieved through a "Virtual Tenant" that masks the complexity.
146: 
147: | Mode | Behavior |
148: |------|----------|
149: | **Single-Tenant** | `TenantId` hardcoded to `Default`; tenant management UI hidden |
150: | **Multi-Tenant** | `TenantId` resolved from subdomain/header; full tenant management |
151: 
152: ### Runtime Mode Switching
153: 
154: The deployment mode can be changed at runtime without application restart:
155: 1. Instance Admin toggles setting in dashboard
156: 2. Database updated, cache invalidated
157: 3. Next request uses new mode
158: 4. UI adapts automatically (tenant menu appears/disappears)
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: ## Onboarding Patterns
163: 
164: ### Instance Admin First-Run
165: 
166: When the platform is first installed:
167: 1. First user becomes Instance Admin
168: 2. Wizard asks deployment purpose (Dedicated vs. SaaS)
169: 3. Module selection for the instance
170: 4. Default tenant configuration
171: 
172: ### Tenant Registration Policies
173: 
174: | Policy | Description |
175: |--------|-------------|
176: | **Open** | Self-service registration via public form |
177: | **Invite-Only** | Instance Admin sends invitation link |
178: | **Sales-Gated** | Request must be approved by sales team |
179: | **Closed** | No new tenants (maintenance mode) |
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## Related Documentation
184: 
185: - **[ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md](ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md)** - Detailed authority model
186: - **[DEPLOYMENT_MODES.md](DEPLOYMENT_MODES.md)** - Single vs multi-tenant deployment
187: - **[EXTENSIBILITY.md](EXTENSIBILITY.md)** - Module and aspect architecture
188: - **[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** - Overall system architecture
189: 
190: ## Implementation Reference
191: 
192: For code patterns and implementation details:
193: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** skill - Tenant query filters
194: - **`auth-patterns`** skill - Tenant context extraction
195: - **`clean-architecture-rules`** skill - Layer boundaries
````

## File: docs/NAMING_CONVENTIONS.md
````markdown
  1: # Naming Conventions
  2: 
  3: > Comprehensive naming patterns used across the codebase.
  4: > Follow these exactly when creating new files, classes, or members.
  5: > Last Updated: February 2026
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## Project Naming
 10: 
 11: | Project | Pattern | Purpose |
 12: |---|---|---|
 13: | `Explore.Domain` | `Explore.{Layer}` | Core domain entities |
 14: | `Explore.Application` | `Explore.{Layer}` | Business logic / CQRS |
 15: | `Explore.Persistence` | `Explore.{Layer}` | Data access / EF Core |
 16: | `Explore.Infrastructure` | `Explore.{Layer}` | External services |
 17: | `Explore.API` | `Explore.{Layer}` | Web API host |
 18: | `Explore.Blazor` | `Explore.Blazor` | Blazor Server host |
 19: | `Explore.Blazor.Client` | `Explore.Blazor.Client` | Blazor WASM client |
 20: | `Explore.Secrets` | `Explore.{Library}` | Standalone library |
 21: | `Event.Application.UnitTests` | `Event.{Layer}.{TestType}` | Test projects (legacy "Event" prefix) |
 22: | `Event.Architecture.Tests` | `Event.Architecture.Tests` | Architecture fitness tests |
 23: 
 24: **Note:** Main projects use the `Explore.*` prefix (historical naming, will be renamed to `Event.*` in the future). Test projects already use `Event.*` prefix.
 25: 
 26: ---
 27: 
 28: ## File Naming
 29: 
 30: All source files use **PascalCase** matching the primary class/type name:
 31: 
 32: | File type | Pattern | Example |
 33: |---|---|---|
 34: | Entity | `{EntityName}.cs` | `Event.cs`, `Organization.cs` |
 35: | Enum | `{EntityName}Enum.cs` | `EventTypeEnum.cs`, `EventStatusEnum.cs` |
 36: | Interface | `I{Name}.cs` | `IEventRepository.cs`, `ITenantContext.cs` |
 37: | DTO | `{Prefix}{EntityName}Dto.cs` | `CreateEventDto.cs`, `EventListDto.cs` |
 38: | Command | `{Verb}{EntityName}Command.cs` | `CreateEventCommand.cs` |
 39: | Query | `Get{EntityName}{Suffix}Request.cs` | `GetEventListRequest.cs` |
 40: | Handler | `{CommandOrQuery}Handler.cs` | `CreateEventCommandHandler.cs` |
 41: | Repository interface | `I{EntityName}Repository.cs` | `IEventRepository.cs` |
 42: | Repository implementation | `{EntityName}Repository.cs` | `EventRepository.cs` |
 43: | EF Configuration | `{EntityName}Configuration.cs` | `EventConfiguration.cs` |
 44: | Controller | `{EntityName}Controller.cs` | `EventController.cs` |
 45: | Blazor page | `{PageName}.razor` + `{PageName}.razor.cs` | `EventList.razor` |
 46: | Blazor CSS | `{PageName}.razor.css` | `EventList.razor.css` |
 47: | Client service | `{EntityName}Service.cs` | `EventService.cs` |
 48: | Validator | `{Prefix}{EntityName}DtoValidator.cs` | `CreateEventDtoValidator.cs` |
 49: 
 50: ---
 51: 
 52: ## Namespace Conventions
 53: 
 54: **File-scoped namespaces** are required (C# 10+ style):
 55: 
 56: ```
 57: namespace Explore.Application.Features.Events.Handlers.Commands;
 58: ```
 59: 
 60: Namespace structure mirrors folder structure exactly:
 61: 
 62: | Layer | Namespace |
 63: |---|---|
 64: | Domain entities | `Explore.Domain` |
 65: | Domain enums | `Explore.Domain.Enums` |
 66: | Domain interfaces | `Explore.Domain.Interfaces` |
 67: | Application DTOs | `Explore.Application.DTOs.{EntityName}` |
 68: | Application features | `Explore.Application.Features.{EntityNames}.Handlers.{Commands\|Queries}` |
 69: | Application requests | `Explore.Application.Features.{EntityNames}.Requests.{Commands\|Queries}` |
 70: | Application contracts | `Explore.Application.Contracts.{Persistence\|Infrastructure\|Identity}` |
 71: | Persistence repos | `Explore.Persistence.Repositories` |
 72: | Persistence configs | `Explore.Persistence.Configurations.Entities` |
 73: | API controllers | `Explore.API.Controllers` |
 74: | API services | `Explore.API.Services` |
 75: | Blazor client services | `Explore.Blazor.Client.Services` |
 76: | Blazor client pages | `Explore.Blazor.Client.Pages.{Area}` |
 77: 
 78: ---
 79: 
 80: ## Entity Naming
 81: 
 82: ### Primary Entities (Guid PK)
 83: 
 84: Singular noun, PascalCase. One class per file at `Explore.Domain/` root.
 85: 
 86: - `Event`, `Organization`, `Actor`, `User`, `Tenant`, `Location`, `StorageObject`, `Category`, `Tag`
 87: 
 88: ### Lookup Tables (int PK)
 89: 
 90: Singular noun. These are reference data that rarely changes.
 91: 
 92: - `EventType`, `EventStatus`, `EventFormat`, `AudienceAge`, `AudienceGender`
 93: - `Madhab`, `Language`, `VisibilityType`, `RegistrationMode`
 94: - `OrganizationRole`, `OrganizationPosition`, `ActorType`, `FileType`, `DidCustodyType`
 95: 
 96: ### Link/Junction Tables (Composite PK)
 97: 
 98: Named as `{Parent}{Child}` (plural for many-to-many collections):
 99: 
100: - `EventCategories` — Event ↔ Category
101: - `EventTags` — Event ↔ Tag
102: - `EventSessionLanguage` — EventSession ↔ Language
103: - `EventSessionSpeaker` — EventSession ↔ Speaker (User)
104: - `TagTypeTags` — TagType ↔ Tag
105: - `OrganizationMember` — Organization ↔ User (with Role)
106: - `UserRole` — User ↔ Role (per tenant)
107: 
108: **Note:** Some junction table names are plural (`EventCategories`, `EventTags`) while others are singular (`OrganizationMember`, `EventSessionLanguage`). Follow the existing pattern when extending.
109: 
110: ### Aspect Tables (1:1 Optional Extension)
111: 
112: Named as `{Parent}{Module}Aspect`:
113: 
114: - `EventIslamicAspect` — Islamic-specific fields for Event
115: - `EventTechAspect` — Tech-specific fields for Event
116: 
117: ### Settings Entities
118: 
119: - `SystemSetting` — Instance-wide settings (global)
120: - `TenantSetting` — Per-tenant setting overrides
121: - `TenantSettings` — Tenant settings snapshot entity (different from TenantSetting)
122: - `AppSetting` — Application-level settings
123: 
124: ---
125: 
126: ## Enum Naming
127: 
128: Enums are named `{EntityName}Enum` and placed in `Explore.Domain/Enums/`. They mirror the int IDs used in lookup tables:
129: 
130: ```
131: EventTypeEnum.cs       → values: Conference = 1, Workshop = 2, ...
132: EventStatusEnum.cs     → values: Draft = 1, Published = 2, ...
133: AudienceAgeEnum.cs     → values: AllAges = 1, Children = 2, ...
134: ```
135: 
136: Each enum value maps to a lookup table row's int `Id`.
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## DTO Naming
141: 
142: DTOs follow a strict prefix/suffix pattern per entity:
143: 
144: | DTO Purpose | Pattern | Example |
145: |---|---|---|
146: | Full details (read) | `{EntityName}Dto` | `EventDto`, `OrganizationDto` |
147: | List view (read) | `{EntityName}ListDto` | `EventListDto`, `OrganizationListDto` |
148: | Create payload (write) | `Create{EntityName}Dto` | `CreateEventDto` |
149: | Update payload (write) | `Update{EntityName}Dto` | `UpdateEventDto` |
150: 
151: DTOs live in `Explore.Application/DTOs/{EntityName}/` — one folder per entity, all DTOs for that entity in the same folder.
152: 
153: ---
154: 
155: ## CQRS Naming
156: 
157: ### Commands (Write Operations)
158: 
159: | Component | Pattern | Example |
160: |---|---|---|
161: | Command request | `{Verb}{EntityName}Command` | `CreateEventCommand` |
162: | Command handler | `{Verb}{EntityName}CommandHandler` | `CreateEventCommandHandler` |
163: 
164: Common verbs: `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Add`, `Remove`
165: 
166: ### Queries (Read Operations)
167: 
168: | Component | Pattern | Example |
169: |---|---|---|
170: | Query request | `Get{EntityName}{Suffix}Request` | `GetEventListRequest`, `GetEventDetailsRequest` |
171: | Query handler | `Get{EntityName}{Suffix}RequestHandler` | `GetEventListRequestHandler` |
172: 
173: Common suffixes: `List`, `Details`, `ById`, `By{RelatedEntity}`
174: 
175: ### Folder Structure
176: 
177: Features are pluralized: `Events/`, `Organizations/`, `AudienceAges/`
178: 
179: ```
180: Features/{EntityNames}/
181: ├── Requests/
182: │   ├── Commands/    — {Verb}{EntityName}Command.cs
183: │   └── Queries/     — Get{EntityName}{Suffix}Request.cs
184: └── Handlers/
185:     ├── Commands/    — {Verb}{EntityName}CommandHandler.cs
186:     └── Queries/     — Get{EntityName}{Suffix}RequestHandler.cs
187: ```
188: 
189: ---
190: 
191: ## Repository Naming
192: 
193: | Component | Pattern | Example |
194: |---|---|---|
195: | Interface | `I{EntityName}Repository` | `IEventRepository` |
196: | Implementation | `{EntityName}Repository` | `EventRepository` |
197: | Generic base | `IGenericRepository<T, TKey>` | `GenericRepository<T, TKey>` |
198: 
199: Interfaces in: `Explore.Application/Contracts/Persistence/`
200: Implementations in: `Explore.Persistence/Repositories/`
201: 
202: ---
203: 
204: ## Controller Naming
205: 
206: Controllers are named `{EntityName}Controller` and placed in `Explore.API/Controllers/`. They map 1:1 with domain aggregates:
207: 
208: | Controller | Route |
209: |---|---|
210: | `EventController` | `api/v1/event` |
211: | `OrganizationController` | `api/v1/organization` |
212: | `EventSessionController` | `api/v1/eventsession` |
213: 
214: Route convention: `api/v1/[controller]` (controller name lowercased, no hyphens).
215: 
216: ---
217: 
218: ## Blazor Page Naming
219: 
220: Pages use PascalCase and are organized by area:
221: 
222: | Area | Page pattern | Example |
223: |---|---|---|
224: | Event pages | `Pages/Event/{Action}.razor` | `EventList.razor`, `CreateEvent.razor` |
225: | Organization | `Pages/Organization/{Action}.razor` | `OrganizationDetails.razor` |
226: | Admin | `Pages/Admin/{Area}.razor` | `LookupTables.razor` |
227: 
228: Each page has a code-behind: `{PageName}.razor.cs` (partial class).
229: Optional scoped CSS: `{PageName}.razor.css`.
230: 
231: ---
232: 
233: ## Service Naming (Blazor Client)
234: 
235: Client services follow `{EntityName}Service` with interface `I{EntityName}Service`:
236: 
237: | Service | Purpose |
238: |---|---|
239: | `EventService` / `IEventService` | Event API calls |
240: | `OrganizationService` / `IOrganizationService` | Organization API calls |
241: | `LookupCacheService` / `ILookupCacheService` | Caches lookup table data |
242: | `AuthStateService` / `IAuthStateService` | Centralized auth state |
243: | `BffClient` | Low-level BFF HTTP calls with XSRF |
244: | `ImageStorageService` / `IImageStorageService` | S3 presigned URL uploads |
245: 
246: ---
247: 
248: ## Database Column Naming
249: 
250: EF Core is configured with **snake_case naming convention** (via `UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention()`):
251: 
252: | C# Property | Database Column |
253: |---|---|
254: | `EventTypeId` | `event_type_id` |
255: | `CreatedAt` | `created_at` |
256: | `IsDeleted` | `is_deleted` |
257: | `TenantId` | `tenant_id` |
258: 
259: Table names are also snake_case plurals of the entity name.
260: 
261: ---
262: 
263: ## Seed Data ID Conventions
264: 
265: - **Lookup tables** (int PK): IDs defined in enum files, seeded via `HasData()` in EF configurations
266: - **Main entities** (Guid PK): IDs defined in `SeedIds.cs` using deterministic **UUIDv7** format
267: - UUIDv7 pattern: `018e4e5c-xxxx-7xxx-8xxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` (time-ordered, unique per entity type)
268: - Seed IDs must never change once used in production
269: 
270: ---
271: 
272: ## Test Naming
273: 
274: ### Test Projects
275: 
276: | Project | Test type | Framework |
277: |---|---|---|
278: | `Event.Application.UnitTests` | Unit | TUnit |
279: | `Event.Domain.UnitTests` | Unit | TUnit |
280: | `Event.Architecture.Tests` | Architecture | TUnit |
281: | `Event.Persistence.IntegrationTests` | Integration | TUnit |
282: | `Event.API.IntegrationTests` | Integration | TUnit |
283: | `Explore.Blazor.Client.Tests` | Component | bUnit + TUnit |
284: | `Explore.Secrets.UnitTests` | Unit | TUnit |
285: 
286: ### Test Class Naming
287: 
288: Test classes mirror the class under test with a `Tests` suffix:
289: 
290: - `CreateEventCommandHandlerTests` — Tests `CreateEventCommandHandler`
291: - `EventRepositoryTests` — Tests `EventRepository`
292: - `CleanArchitectureTests` — Architecture rule tests
293: 
294: ### Test Method Naming
295: 
296: Methods use descriptive names: `{Method}_{Scenario}_{ExpectedResult}`
297: 
298: ---
299: 
300: ## Configuration Naming
301: 
302: ### EF Core Configuration
303: 
304: | Component | Pattern | Location |
305: |---|---|---|
306: | Entity config class | `{EntityName}Configuration` | `Configurations/Entities/` |
307: | Implements | `IEntityTypeConfiguration<{EntityName}>` | — |
308: 
309: ### DI Registration
310: 
311: | Registration file | Pattern |
312: |---|---|
313: | `PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs` | `CongfigurePersistenceServices()` (note: typo is intentional/existing) |
314: | `InfrastructureServicesRegistration.cs` | `ConfigureInfrastructureServices()` |
315: | `Explore.Blazor.Client/Program.cs` | Direct service registration |
316: | `Explore.API/Program.cs` | Calls all registration methods |
317: 
318: ---
319: 
320: ## Constants and Settings Key Naming
321: 
322: Governance setting keys use dot-separated hierarchical names:
323: 
324: ```
325: Deployment.Mode
326: Events.MaxSessionsPerEvent
327: Events.RequireApproval
328: Modules.Islamic.Enabled
329: Modules.Tech.Enabled
330: Branding.DisplayName
331: Domains.InstanceBaseDomain
332: ```
333: 
334: Defined in `Explore.Domain/Constants/GovernanceSettingKeys.cs`.
335: 
336: ---
337: 
338: ## Summary: Quick Rules
339: 
340: 1. **Entities** = singular PascalCase, one per file at Domain root
341: 2. **Enums** = `{Entity}Enum` in `Domain/Enums/`
342: 3. **DTOs** = `{Prefix}{Entity}Dto` in `Application/DTOs/{Entity}/`
343: 4. **Commands** = `{Verb}{Entity}Command` in `Features/{Entities}/Requests/Commands/`
344: 5. **Queries** = `Get{Entity}{Suffix}Request` in `Features/{Entities}/Requests/Queries/`
345: 6. **Handlers** = mirror command/query name + `Handler` suffix
346: 7. **Repositories** = `I{Entity}Repository` (interface) / `{Entity}Repository` (impl)
347: 8. **Controllers** = `{Entity}Controller`, route `api/v1/[controller]`
348: 9. **Blazor pages** = `{Action}{Entity}.razor` or `{Entity}{Action}.razor` (varies by area)
349: 10. **Client services** = `{Entity}Service` / `I{Entity}Service`
350: 11. **DB columns** = snake_case (automatic via EF Core convention)
351: 12. **Namespaces** = file-scoped, mirror folder structure exactly
````

## File: docs/PROJECT.md
````markdown
  1: ## 1. Project Overview
  2: 
  3: ## What is ISLAMU Event?
  4: 
  5: **ISLAMU Event** (also known as ISLAMU Explore or Event Explorer) is an **open-source event discovery platform**.
  6: 
  7: The long-term vision includes **ATProto-first federation** with an **ActivityPub gateway**, but HTTP federation endpoints are **not currently implemented** in `Explore.API`.
  8: 
  9: ## Core Value Proposition
 10: 
 11: | Component | Value |
 12:   |-----------|-------|
 13: | **Software** | Multi-tenant federated event platform (AGPL) |
 14: | **Primary Instance** | Trusted Islamic event directory with verification |
 15: | **Filtering System** | Culturally-appropriate discovery (age, gender, madhab) |
 16: 
 17: ## Organizational Context
 18: 
 19: - **Organization**: ISLAMU Non Profit Organization (Islamic Software Lighthouse Alliance of the Muslim Ummah)
 20: - **Legal Entity**: Belgian non-profit organization ASBL (Association sans but lucratif)
 21: - **GitHub Organization**: `islamu-ngo`
 22: - **Repository**: `https://github.com/islamu-ngo/explore`
 23: - **License**: AGPL-3.0
 24: 
 25: ---
 26: 
 27: # Strategic Context
 28: 
 29: ## Ecosystem Architecture
 30: 
 31: ```
 32: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 38: │  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │   │
 39: │  │  • Islamic events globally                                  │   │
 40: │  │  • Verified actors (fact-checked)                           │   │
 41: │  │  • User-submitted events (flagged as unverified)            │   │
 42: │  │  • Strike/ban system for policy violations                  │   │

 44: │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │

 50: │  │ Instance     │  │ Instance     │  │ Instance     │              │

101: # Core Features

103: ## Two-Tier Verification System
104: 
105: ```
106: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
107: │                    VERIFICATION SYSTEM                              │
108: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
109: │                                                                     │
110: │  TIER 1: User-Submitted Events                                      │
111: │  ├── Anyone can create account                                      │
112: │  ├── Can post events immediately                                    │
113: │  ├── Events marked as "User Reported"                               │
114: │  ├── Subject to community moderation                                │
115: │  └── Strike/ban system for violations                               │
116: │                                                                     │
117: │  TIER 2: Verified Organizations                                     │
118: │  ├── Application required                                           │
119: │  └── Fact-checking process:                                         │

121: │                                                                     │
122: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

124: 
125: ## Advanced Filtering System
126: 
127: | Filter | Options | Description |
128: |--------|---------|-------------|
129: | **Audience Age** | Children, Youth, Adults, Seniors, All Ages | Target demographic |
130: | **Gender** | Men-only, Women-only, Mixed, Family | Audience type |
131: | **Location** | Country, Region, City, Radius | Geographic filtering with PostGIS |
132: | **Language** | Arabic, English, French, etc. | Event language |
133: | **Event Type** | Webinar, Conference | Event Type |
134: | **Madhab** | Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali | Islamic jurisprudence school |
135: | **Category** | Aqidah, Fiqh, Tafsir, Hadith, etc. | Event classification |
136: | **Tag** | Mohammed Hijab, Mufti Menk etc... | Event tags |
137: | **TagType** | Person, Channel, oeuvres | Tag classification |
138: | **TagTypeTags** | Specific tags within TagType | e.g., Person → Mohammed Hijab |
139: | **Event Format** | In-person Local (physical), Digital (online), Hybrid | Event format |
140: | **Date/Time** | Upcoming, This Week, This Month, Custom | Temporal filtering |
141: | **Verification** | Verified only, All | Trust level |
142: 
143: ## Liturgical Temporal Engine
144: 
145: **Dynamic Prayer-Relative Scheduling**:
146: 
147: - Events can be scheduled relative to prayer times (e.g., "15 minutes after Maghrib")
148: - exact times based on event geolocation using Third-party API
149: 
150: ## Moderation System
151: 
152: Still todo
153: 
154: ## Data Portability
155: 
156: Export formats supported:
157: - **iCal/ICS**: Standard calendar format for events
158: - **CSV**: Attendee lists, organizations, bulk data
159: - **ActivityPub-native** (planned): Federation-compatible JSON-LD
160: - **Full database dump**: Complete data export for self-hosters
161:

## File: docs/RENDER_POLICIES.md
````markdown
  1: # Render Policies
  2: 
  3: > **Policy-Based UI Rendering Architecture**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes how the platform manages Blazor render modes dynamically
  6: > based on policies, not hardcoded configurations.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform uses a **Policy-Based Render Mode System** that separates technical implementation (Server, WebAssembly, Auto) from business decisions (which pages need which level of interactivity). This enables Instance Admins to optimize resource usage without code changes.
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## The Problem
 19: 
 20: ### Traditional Approach Issues
 21: 
 22: - Render modes hardcoded per component
 23: - Changing modes requires code deployment
 24: - One-size-fits-all doesn't match varied tenant needs
 25: - Resource optimization is developer-driven, not operations-driven
 26: 
 27: ### Policy-Based Solution
 28: 
 29: - Pages classified by logical type, not technical mode
 30: - Policies map logical types to render modes
 31: - Instance Admin controls the mapping
 32: - Tenant Admin may override (if permitted)
 33: 
 34: ---
 35: 
 36: ## Page Classification System
 37: 
 38: ### Logical Page Types
 39: 
 40: Pages are tagged with a logical classification, independent of render technology:
 41: 
 42: | Type | Characteristics | Examples |
 43: |------|-----------------|----------|
 44: | **Content** | Read-heavy, cacheable, SEO-important | Listings, blogs, public profiles |
 45: | **Operational** | Interactive, form-heavy, real-time updates | Dashboards, editors, admin panels |
 46: | **Transactional** | Critical operations, payment flows | Checkout, registration completion |
 47: | **Static** | Rarely changes, no interactivity | About, legal, help pages |
 48: 
 49: ### Classification Guidelines
 50: 
 51: | Criteria | Content | Operational |
 52: |----------|---------|-------------|
 53: | User interaction | Low | High |
 54: | Data freshness | Can be stale | Must be current |
 55: | SEO importance | High | Low |
 56: | Server load | Low per view | Higher per session |
 57: 
 58: ---
 59: 
 60: ## Render Mode Options
 61: 
 62: ### Available Modes
 63: 
 64: | Mode | Description | Best For |
 65: |------|-------------|----------|
 66: | **Static** | Pre-rendered, no interactivity | Content pages, SEO |
 67: | **Server** | SignalR connection, server-side execution | Operational pages, complex logic |
 68: | **WebAssembly** | Client-side execution | Offline capability, reduced server load |
 69: | **Auto** | Server initially, transitions to WASM | Best of both worlds |
 70: 
 71: ### Mode Trade-offs
 72: 
 73: | Factor | Static | Server | WASM | Auto |
 74: |--------|--------|--------|------|------|
 75: | Initial load | ⚡ Fastest | Fast | Slow | Fast |
 76: | Interactivity | ❌ None | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full |
 77: | Server resources | ⚡ Minimal | ⬆️ Higher | ⚡ Minimal | Medium |
 78: | Offline support | ❌ No | ❌ No | ✅ Yes | ⚡ Partial |
 79: | SEO | ✅ Best | ✅ Good | ⚠️ Challenging | ✅ Good |
 80: 
 81: ---
 82: 
 83: ## Policy Definition
 84: 
 85: ### Resolution Matrix
 86: 
 87: Instance Admin defines how page types map to render modes:
 88: 
 89: | Policy Name | Content | Operational | Transactional | Use Case |
 90: |-------------|---------|-------------|---------------|----------|
 91: | **Performance Saver** | Static | WASM | Server | Free tier, low server cost |
 92: | **Premium Fast** | Static | Server | Server | Paid tier, responsiveness priority |
 93: | **Modern Edge** | Auto | Auto | Auto | Modern devices, best UX |
 94: | **Compatibility** | Static | Server | Server | Legacy browser support |
 95: 
 96: ### Policy Assignment
 97: 
 98: | Level | Can Assign | Constraints |
 99: |-------|------------|-------------|
100: | System Default | Implicit | Fallback only |
101: | Instance | Instance Admin | Any combination |
102: | Tenant | Tenant Admin | Within allowed set |
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## Implementation Architecture
107: 
108: ### Policy Resolution Flow
109: 
110: 1. **Page Request** → User navigates to page
111: 2. **Type Lookup** → System identifies page's logical type
112: 3. **Policy Check** → Resolver queries current policy
113: 4. **Mode Selection** → Policy maps type to render mode
114: 5. **Rendering** → Page renders with selected mode
115: 
116: ### Policy Service Interface
117: 
118: The policy service answers: "Given this page type and context, what render mode should be used?"
119: 
120: **Inputs**:
121: - Page type (Content, Operational, etc.)
122: - Tenant context (if any)
123: - Device hints (optional)
124: - User preferences (optional)
125: 
126: **Output**:
127: - Render mode to apply
128: 
129: ### Dynamic Wrapper Component
130: 
131: A wrapper component at the layout level:
132: 1. Reads the policy for the current page type
133: 2. Applies the resolved render mode
134: 3. Renders the actual page content
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ## Configuration Model
139: 
140: ### Instance-Level Settings
141: 
142: | Setting | Values | Default |
143: |---------|--------|---------|
144: | Default Policy | Policy name | "Modern Edge" |
145: | Allow Tenant Override | Boolean | true |
146: | Allowed Tenant Policies | Policy list | All |
147: 
148: ### Tenant-Level Settings
149: 
150: | Setting | Values | Constraint |
151: |---------|--------|------------|
152: | Active Policy | Policy name | Must be in allowed set |
153: | Custom Mappings | Type → Mode | If customization enabled |
154: 
155: ---
156: 
157: ## Optimization Strategies
158: 
159: ### Resource-Based Policies
160: 
161: | Tenant Tier | Recommended Policy | Rationale |
162: |-------------|-------------------|-----------|
163: | Free | Performance Saver | Minimize server usage |
164: | Standard | Modern Edge | Balanced experience |
165: | Premium | Premium Fast | Best responsiveness |
166: | Enterprise | Custom | Tailored to needs |
167: 
168: ### Time-Based Policies
169: 
170: Policies can vary by time of day or load conditions:
171: 
172: | Condition | Policy | Rationale |
173: |-----------|--------|-----------|
174: | Peak hours | Performance Saver | Reduce server strain |
175: | Off-peak | Premium Fast | Better UX when capacity available |
176: | High load | Performance Saver | Graceful degradation |
177: 
178: ---
179: 
180: ## Migration Path
181: 
182: ### From Hardcoded to Policy-Based
183: 
184: 1. **Audit** - Document current render mode per component
185: 2. **Classify** - Assign logical type to each page
186: 3. **Create Baseline** - Define policy matching current behavior
187: 4. **Implement Wrapper** - Add policy resolution to layout
188: 5. **Test** - Verify equivalent behavior
189: 6. **Enable Policies** - Expose policy selection to admins
190: 7. **Optimize** - Create additional policies for different scenarios
191: 
192: ---
193: 
194: ## Related Documentation
195: 
196: - **[BLAZOR.md](BLAZOR.md)** - Blazor architecture overview
197: - **[MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md)** - Tenant configuration
198: - **[ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md](ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md)** - Policy authority
199: 
200: ## Implementation Reference
201: 
202: For code patterns:
203: - **`blazor-bff-patterns`** skill - BFF and rendering
204: - **`blazor-ui-conventions`** skill - Component patterns
````

## File: docs/SECURITY.md
````markdown
 1: # Security Architecture
 2: 
 3: This document provides a high-level overview of the security architecture for the ISLAMU Event platform.
 4: 
 5: For detailed implementation patterns, code examples, and specific conventions, refer to the **`auth-patterns` skill**.
 6: 
 7: ## 1. Authentication Strategy: Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
 8: 
 9: The project employs a **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** security model to provide a high level of security by ensuring that no tokens are ever exposed to the end-user's browser.
10: 
11: **Protocol**: OpenID Connect (OIDC) / OAuth 2.0  
12: **Provider**: Keycloak
13: 
14: ### Conceptual Flow
15: 
16: The authentication flow is designed to separate the concerns of browser session management from backend API authorization.
17: 
18: ```mermaid
19: sequenceDiagram
20:     participant Browser (Blazor WASM)
21:     participant BFF (Blazor Server)
22:     participant Keycloak
23:     participant API (Backend)
24: 
25:     Browser->>+BFF: User clicks "Login"
26:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Initiates OIDC Authorization Code Flow
27:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Redirects with Authorization Code
28:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Exchanges Code for Tokens (Access + Refresh)
29:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Returns JWTs
30:     BFF-->>-Browser: Stores tokens in a secure, HttpOnly cookie & redirects
31: 
32:     Browser->>+BFF: Makes API call
33:     BFF->>+API: YARP proxy attaches JWT Bearer token
34:     API->>API: Validates JWT
35:     API-->>-BFF: Returns data
36:     BFF-->>-Browser: Returns data
37: ```
38: 
39: ### Key Architectural Principles
40: 
41: *   **`Explore.Blazor` (The BFF)** is the only component that communicates directly with Keycloak. It manages the user's session using a secure, server-side, `HttpOnly` cookie.
42: *   **`Explore.Blazor.Client` (The Frontend)** is completely unaware of OIDC or JWTs. It operates like a traditional web application, automatically sending the session cookie with every request to its backend (the BFF).
43: *   **`Explore.API` (The Backend Resource)** is a stateless service. It only accepts JWT Bearer tokens for authorization and has no knowledge of the user's session cookie. This allows the API to be used by other clients (e.g., mobile apps, other services) in the future.
44: 
45: ## 2. Authorization Strategy
46: 
47: ### Endpoint-Level Authorization
48: 
49: A simple and strict convention is followed for securing API endpoints:
50: *   **Read operations (`GET`)** are generally public and decorated with `[AllowAnonymous]`.
51: *   **Write operations (`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`)** are protected and require a valid token, enforced with `[Authorize]`.
52: 
53: ### Resource-Level Authorization
54: 
55: Fine-grained, resource-level authorization (e.g., "can this user edit *this specific* event?") is the responsibility of the **Application Layer**, typically within the MediatR handlers. This logic is not handled at the controller level.
56: 
57: ### Future: Policy-Based Authorization (Cerbos)
58: 
59: The architecture is designed to incorporate a dedicated policy decision point (PDP) like Cerbos in the future. However, **Cerbos is not currently integrated**. All authorization logic is currently implemented within the application code.
60: 
61: ---
62: For implementation details, see the `auth-patterns` skill.
````

109: 
110: ### Common Types
111: 
112: | Placeholder | Description | Example Value |
113: |-------------|-------------|---------------|
114: | `{ResponseType}` | Command response type | `BaseCommandResponse<Guid>` |
115: | `{ListDtoType}` | List DTO type | `List<{Entity}ListDto>` |
116: | `{PaginatedType}` | Paginated response type | `PaginatedResult<{Entity}ListDto>` |
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: ## 5. Layer Placeholders
121: 
122: ### Namespace Patterns
123: 
124: | Placeholder | Expands To |
125: |-------------|------------|
126: | `{Project.Domain.Namespace}` | `{Project}.Domain` |
127: | `{Project.Application.Namespace}` | `{Project}.Application` |
128: | `{Project.Application.Features.Namespace}` | `{Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}` |
129: | `{Project.Persistence.Namespace}` | `{Project}.Persistence` |
130: | `{Project.API.Namespace}` | `{Project}.API` |
131: 
132: ### File Path Patterns
133: 
134: | Placeholder | Example Path |
135: |-------------|--------------|
136: | `{Entity.Command.Path}` | `{Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Requests/Commands/` |
137: | `{Entity.Query.Path}` | `{Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Requests/Queries/` |
138: | `{Entity.Handler.Path}` | `{Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/` |
139: | `{Entity.Dto.Path}` | `{Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/` |
140: | `{Entity.Validator.Path}` | `{Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/Validators/` |
141: | `{Entity.Repository.Path}` | `{Project}.Persistence/Repositories/` |
142: | `{Entity.Controller.Path}` | `{Project}.API/Controllers/` |
143: 
144: ---
145: 
146: ## 6. CQRS Placeholders
147: 
148: ### Commands
149: 
150: | Placeholder | Expands To | Example |
151: |-------------|------------|---------|
152: | `Create{Entity}Command` | Create command class | `CreateEventCommand` |
153: | `Update{Entity}Command` | Update command class | `UpdateEventCommand` |
154: | `Delete{Entity}Command` | Delete command class | `DeleteEventCommand` |
155: | `Create{Entity}CommandHandler` | Create handler | `CreateEventCommandHandler` |
156: 
157: ### Queries
158: 
159: | Placeholder | Expands To | Example |
160: |-------------|------------|---------|
161: | `Get{Entity}ListRequest` | List query | `GetEventListRequest` |
162: | `Get{Entity}DetailsRequest` | Details query | `GetEventDetailsRequest` |
163: | `Get{Entities}By{RelatedEntity}Request` | Filter query | `GetEventsByOrganizationRequest` |
164: 
165: ### DTOs
166: 
167: | Placeholder | Expands To | Example |
168: |-------------|------------|---------|
169: | `{Entity}Dto` | Full details DTO | `EventDto` |
170: | `{Entity}ListDto` | List view DTO | `EventListDto` |
171: | `Create{Entity}Dto` | Create payload | `CreateEventDto` |
172: | `Update{Entity}Dto` | Update payload | `UpdateEventDto` |
173: 
174: ### Validators
175: 
176: | Placeholder | Expands To | Example |
177: |-------------|------------|---------|
178: | `Create{Entity}DtoValidator` | Create validator | `CreateEventDtoValidator` |
179: | `Update{Entity}DtoValidator` | Update validator | `UpdateEventDtoValidator` |
180: 
181: ### Repositories
182: 
183: | Placeholder | Expands To | Example |
184: |-------------|------------|---------|
185: | `I{Entity}Repository` | Repository interface | `IEventRepository` |
186: | `{Entity}Repository` | Repository implementation | `EventRepository` |
187: 
188: ---
189: 
190: ## 7. Substitution Examples
191: 
192: ### Example 1: Event Management System
193: 
194: **Substitutions:**
195: ```
196: {Project}        = Explore
197: {Entity}         = Event
198: {Entities}       = Events
199: {RelatedEntity}  = Organization
200: {LookupEntity}   = EventType
201: {IdType}         = Guid
202: {LookupIdType}   = int
203: ```
204: 
205: **Template Code:**
206: ```csharp
207: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
208: 
209: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
210: {
211:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
212:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity}Repository _{relatedEntity}Repository;
213: 
214:     // ...
215: }
216: ```
217: 
218: **Becomes:**
219: ```csharp
220: namespace Explore.Application.Features.Events.Handlers.Commands;
221: 
222: public class CreateEventCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateEventCommand, BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>
223: {
224:     private readonly IEventRepository _eventRepository;
225:     private readonly IOrganizationRepository _organizationRepository;
226: 
227:     // ...
228: }
229: ```
230: 
231: ### Example 2: E-Commerce System
232: 
233: **Substitutions:**
234: ```
235: {Project}        = ECommerce
236: {Entity}         = Order
237: {Entities}       = Orders
238: {RelatedEntity}  = Customer
239: {ChildEntity}    = OrderItem
240: {LookupEntity}   = OrderStatus
241: {IdType}         = Guid
242: {LookupIdType}   = int
243: ```
244: 
245: **Template Code:**
246: ```csharp
247: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
248: {
249:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}By{RelatedEntity}({IdType} {relatedEntity}Id)
250:     {
251:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
252:             .Include(e => e.{ChildEntities})
253:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
254:             .Where(e => e.{RelatedEntity}Id == {relatedEntity}Id)
255:             .ToListAsync();
256:     }
257: }
258: ```
259: 
260: **Becomes:**
261: ```csharp
262: public class OrderRepository : GenericRepository<Order, Guid>, IOrderRepository
263: {
264:     public async Task<List<Order>> GetOrdersByCustomer(Guid customerId)
265:     {
266:         return await _dbContext.Orders
267:             .Include(e => e.OrderItems)
268:             .Include(e => e.OrderStatus)
269:             .Where(e => e.CustomerId == customerId)
270:             .ToListAsync();
271:     }
272: }
273: ```
274: 
275: ---
276: 
277: ## 8. Best Practices
278: 
279: ### When Creating New Documentation
280: 
281: 1. **Always use placeholders** for entity-specific names
282: 2. **Provide substitution tables** at the top of each document
283: 3. **Include concrete examples** in "Implementation Example" sections
284: 4. **Mark project-specific sections** clearly
285: 
286: ### Substitution Table Template
287: 
288: Add this to any document that uses placeholders:
289: 
290: ```markdown
291: ## Placeholder Substitutions
292: 
293: | Placeholder | Replace With |
294: |-------------|--------------|
295: | `{Project}` | Your solution name |
296: | `{Entity}` | Your main entity |
297: | `{Entities}` | Plural form |
298: | `{RelatedEntity}` | Related entity for FK |
299: | `{IdType}` | `Guid` (recommended) or `int` |
300: ```
301: 
302: ### Naming Conventions
303: 
304: | Type | Convention | Example |
305: |------|------------|---------|
306: | Entity | PascalCase, singular | `Event`, `Order` |
307: | DbSet | PascalCase, plural | `Events`, `Orders` |
308: | Repository | I{Entity}Repository | `IEventRepository` |
309: | Controller | {Entity}Controller | `EventController` |
310: | DTO | {Entity}Dto, {Entity}ListDto | `EventDto`, `EventListDto` |
311: | Command | {Verb}{Entity}Command | `CreateEventCommand` |
312: | Query | Get{Entity}*Request | `GetEventListRequest` |
313: | Handler | {Command/Query}Handler | `CreateEventCommandHandler` |
314: | Validator | {Dto}Validator | `CreateEventDtoValidator` |
315: 
316: ---
317: 
318: ## Design Principles Reference
319: 
320: These principles guide all documentation and should be followed when implementing:
321: 
322: ### SOLID Principles
323: 
324: | Principle | Application |
325: |-----------|-------------|
326: | **S**ingle Responsibility | Each handler handles one command/query |
327: | **O**pen/Closed | Use interfaces for extension |
328: | **L**iskov Substitution | Repositories implement interfaces correctly |
329: | **I**nterface Segregation | Small, focused repository interfaces |
330: | **D**ependency Inversion | Depend on abstractions (interfaces) |
331: 
332: ### Clean Architecture
333: 
334: | Rule | Enforcement |
335: |------|-------------|
336: | Dependencies flow inward | Domain has no dependencies |
337: | Entities are framework-agnostic | No EF Core in Domain |
338: | Use cases in Application | Business logic in handlers |
339: | Controllers are thin | Only HTTP ↔ MediatR |
340: 
341: ### Clean Code
342: 
343: | Principle | Example |
344: |-----------|---------|
345: | **DRY** | Use `GenericRepository<T, TId>` |
346: | **KISS** | Simple handlers, one responsibility |
347: | **YAGNI** | Don't add unused abstractions |
348: | Meaningful names | `GetEventsWithDetails()` not `GetData()` |
349: 
350: ---
351: 
352: ## Related Documentation
353: 
354: - **[GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md)** - Coding conventions (project-agnostic)
355: - **[QUICK_REFERENCE.md](QUICK_REFERENCE.md)** - Critical rules summary
356: - **[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** - System architecture patterns
357: 
358: ---
359: 
360: ## Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
361: 
362: This repository (`Explore`) uses the following substitutions:
363: 
364: | Placeholder | ISLAMU Event Value |
365: |-------------|-------------------|
366: | `{Project}` | `Explore` |
367: | `{Project.Domain}` | `Explore.Domain` |
368: | `{Project.Application}` | `Explore.Application` |
369: | `{Project.Persistence}` | `Explore.Persistence` |
370: | `{Project.API}` | `Explore.API` |
371: | `{Project.Blazor}` | `Explore.Blazor` |
372: | `{DbContext}` | `ExploreDbContext` |
373: | `{IdType}` | `Guid` |
374: | `{LookupIdType}` | `int` |
375: 
376: **Sample Entities:**
377: - `{Entity}` = `Event`, `Organization`, `User`, `EventSession`
378: - `{LookupEntity}` = `EventType`, `EventStatus`, `Madhab`, `AudienceAge`
379: - `{LinkEntity}` = `EventCategories`, `EventTags`, `OrganizationMembers`
````

````csharp
 1: namespace Event.Domain.UnitTests.Interfaces;
 2: 
 3: using Explore.Domain;
 4: using Explore.Domain.Interfaces;
 5: 
 6: public class InterfaceImplementationTests
 7: {
 8:     [Test]
 9:     public async Task IAuditableEntity_Implementations_ExposeExpectedProperties()
10:     {
11:         var entityTypes = GetConcreteImplementations<IAuditableEntity>();
12: 
13:         await Assert.That(entityTypes.Length > 0).IsTrue();
14: 
15:         foreach (var entityType in entityTypes)
16:         {
17:             await Assert.That(HasProperty(entityType, nameof(IAuditableEntity.CreatedAt), typeof(DateTime))).IsTrue();
18:             await Assert.That(HasProperty(entityType, nameof(IAuditableEntity.CreatedBy), typeof(Guid?))).IsTrue();
19:             await Assert.That(HasProperty(entityType, nameof(IAuditableEntity.UpdatedAt), typeof(DateTime?))).IsTrue();
20:             await Assert.That(HasProperty(entityType, nameof(IAuditableEntity.UpdatedBy), typeof(Guid?))).IsTrue();
21:         }
22:     }
23: 
24:     [Test]
25:     public async Task ISoftDeletable_Implementations_ExposeExpectedProperties()
26:     {
27:         var entityTypes = GetConcreteImplementations<ISoftDeletable>();
28: 
29:         await Assert.That(entityTypes.Length > 0).IsTrue();
30: 
31:         foreach (var entityType in entityTypes)
32:         {
33:             await Assert.That(HasProperty(entityType, nameof(ISoftDeletable.IsDeleted), typeof(bool))).IsTrue();
34:             await Assert.That(HasProperty(entityType, nameof(ISoftDeletable.DeletedAt), typeof(DateTime?))).IsTrue();
35:             await Assert.That(HasProperty(entityType, nameof(ISoftDeletable.DeletedBy), typeof(Guid?))).IsTrue();
36:         }
37:     }
38: 
39:     [Test]
40:     public async Task ITenantEntity_Implementations_ExposeExpectedProperties()
41:     {
42:         var entityTypes = GetConcreteImplementations<ITenantEntity>();
43: 
44:         await Assert.That(entityTypes.Length > 0).IsTrue();
45: 
46:         foreach (var entityType in entityTypes)
47:         {
48:             await Assert.That(HasProperty(entityType, nameof(ITenantEntity.TenantId), typeof(Guid))).IsTrue();
49:         }
50:     }
51: 
52:     [Test]
53:     public async Task ReflectionScan_IncludesKnownInterfaceImplementations()
54:     {
55:         var auditableTypes = GetConcreteImplementations<IAuditableEntity>();
56:         var softDeletableTypes = GetConcreteImplementations<ISoftDeletable>();
57:         var tenantTypes = GetConcreteImplementations<ITenantEntity>();
58: 
59:         await Assert.That(auditableTypes.Contains(typeof(User))).IsTrue();
60:         await Assert.That(softDeletableTypes.Contains(typeof(User))).IsTrue();
61:         await Assert.That(tenantTypes.Contains(typeof(global::Explore.Domain.Event))).IsTrue();
62:     }
63: 
64:     private static Type[] GetConcreteImplementations<TInterface>()
65:     {
66:         return typeof(global::Explore.Domain.Event).Assembly
67:             .GetTypes()
68:             .Where(type => typeof(TInterface).IsAssignableFrom(type) && !type.IsInterface && !type.IsAbstract)
69:             .ToArray();
70:     }
71: 
72:     private static bool HasProperty(Type type, string propertyName, Type expectedType)
73:     {
74:         var property = type.GetProperty(propertyName);
75:         return property is not null && property.PropertyType == expectedType;
76:     }
77: }

## File: Explore.API/Controllers/InstanceOnboardingController.cs
````csharp
  1: using System;
  2: using System.Security.Claims;
  3: using Explore.Application.DTOs.Onboarding;
  4: using Explore.Application.Features.InstanceOnboarding.Requests.Commands;
  5: using Explore.Application.Features.InstanceOnboarding.Requests.Queries;
  6: using Explore.Application.Responses;
  7: using MediatR;
  8: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
  9: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
 10: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
 11: 
 12: namespace Explore.API.Controllers;
 13: 
 14: [Route("api/v1/[controller]")]
 15: [ApiController]
 16: public class InstanceOnboardingController : ControllerBase
 17: {
 18:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
 19: 
 20:     public InstanceOnboardingController(IMediator mediator)
 21:     {
 22:         _mediator = mediator;
 23:     }
 24: 
 25:     [HttpGet("status")]
 26:     [AllowAnonymous]
 27:     [EndpointSummary("Get Instance Onboarding Status")]
 28:     [EndpointDescription("Returns whether first-run onboarding is completed and whether the current user is instance admin.")]
 29:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(InstanceOnboardingStatusDto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 30:     public async Task<ActionResult<InstanceOnboardingStatusDto>> GetStatus(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 31:     {
 32:         var status = await _mediator.Send(new GetInstanceOnboardingStatusQuery(), cancellationToken);
 33:         return Ok(status);
 34:     }
 35: 
 36:     [HttpGet("settings")]
 37:     [Authorize]
 38:     [EndpointSummary("Get Instance Governance Settings")]
 39:     [EndpointDescription("Returns instance governance settings. If onboarding is already complete, only instance admins can access this endpoint.")]
 40:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(InstanceGovernanceSettingsDto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 41:     [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status403Forbidden)]
 42:     public async Task<ActionResult<InstanceGovernanceSettingsDto>> GetSettings(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 43:     {
 44:         var status = await _mediator.Send(new GetInstanceOnboardingStatusQuery(), cancellationToken);
 45:         if (status.IsCompleted && !status.IsCurrentUserInstanceAdmin)
 46:         {
 47:             return Forbid();
 48:         }
 49: 
 50:         var settings = await _mediator.Send(new GetInstanceGovernanceSettingsQuery(), cancellationToken);
 51:         return Ok(settings);
 52:     }
 53: 
 54:     [HttpPost("complete")]
 55:     [Authorize]
 56:     [EndpointSummary("Complete Instance Onboarding")]
 57:     [EndpointDescription("Completes first-run onboarding, assigns the current user as instance admin, and persists instance governance settings.")]
 58:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 59:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]
 60:     public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Complete([FromBody] InstanceGovernanceSettingsDto settings, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 61:     {
 62:         var currentUserId = GetCurrentUserId();
 63:         if (!currentUserId.HasValue)
 64:         {
 65:             return BadRequest(new BaseCommandResponse<Guid>
 66:             {
 67:                 Success = false,
 68:                 Message = "Invalid user identity."
 69:             });
 70:         }
 71: 
 72:         var command = new CompleteInstanceOnboardingCommand
 73:         {
 74:             UserId = currentUserId.Value,
 75:             Settings = settings
 76:         };
 77: 
 78:         var response = await _mediator.Send(command, cancellationToken);
 79:         if (!response.Success)
 80:         {
 81:             return BadRequest(response);
 82:         }
 83: 
 84:         return Ok(response);
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     [HttpPut("settings")]
 88:     [Authorize]
 89:     [EndpointSummary("Update Instance Governance Settings")]
 90:     [EndpointDescription("Updates instance governance settings at runtime. Requires instance administrator membership.")]
 91:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 92:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]
 93:     [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status403Forbidden)]
 94:     public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> UpdateSettings([FromBody] InstanceGovernanceSettingsDto settings, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 95:     {
 96:         var currentUserId = GetCurrentUserId();
 97:         if (!currentUserId.HasValue)
 98:         {
 99:             return BadRequest(new BaseCommandResponse<Guid>
100:             {
101:                 Success = false,
102:                 Message = "Invalid user identity."
103:             });
104:         }
105: 
106:         var command = new UpdateInstanceGovernanceSettingsCommand
107:         {
108:             UserId = currentUserId.Value,
109:             Settings = settings
110:         };
111: 
112:         var response = await _mediator.Send(command, cancellationToken);
113:         if (!response.Success)
114:         {
115:             if (response.Message.Contains("Only instance administrators", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
116:             {
117:                 return Forbid();
118:             }
119: 
120:             return BadRequest(response);
121:         }
122: 
123:         return Ok(response);
124:     }
125: 
126:     private Guid? GetCurrentUserId()
127:     {
128:         var claim = User.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
129:             ?? User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value
130:             ?? User.FindFirst("sid")?.Value;
131: 
132:         return Guid.TryParse(claim, out var parsedUserId) ? parsedUserId : null;
133:     }
134: }
````

  1: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;

 11: [Route("api/v1/[controller]")]

 28: 
 29: 
 30: 
 31: 
 32:     [HttpGet("available")]

 35:         "Does not filter by tenant - use /enabled for tenant-specific modules.")]
 36:     [AllowAnonymous]
 37:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(IReadOnlyList<ModuleInfo>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]

 39:     {

 44:

 46:

 49:     [EndpointDescription("Returns modules enabled for the current tenant. " +

 47:     [HttpPost("complete")]

 49:     [EndpointSummary("Complete Tenant Onboarding")]
 50:     [EndpointDescription("Completes tenant onboarding and persists tenant policy answers.")]
 51:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 52:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]
 53:     [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status403Forbidden)]
 54:     public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Complete([FromBody] TenantPolicySettingsDto settings, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 55:     {
 56:         var currentUserId = GetCurrentUserId();
 57:         if (!currentUserId.HasValue)
 58:         {
 59:             return BadRequest(new BaseCommandResponse<Guid>
 60:             {
 61:                 Success = false,
 62:                 Message = "Invalid user identity."
 63:             });
 64:         }
 65:

 67:         {
 68:             UserId = currentUserId.Value,
 69:             Settings = settings
 70:         }, cancellationToken);
 71: 
 72:         if (!response.Success)
 73:         {
 74:             if (response.Message.Contains("Only tenant administrators", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
 75:             {
 76:                 return Forbid();
 77:             }
 78: 
 79:             return BadRequest(response);
 80:         }
 81: 
 82:         return Ok(response);

## File: Explore.API/entrypoint.sh
````bash
 1: set -e
 2: 
 3: echo "Starting Explore.API container..."
 4: 
 5: 
 6: if [ -n "$INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID" ] && [ -n "$INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET" ]; then
 7:     echo "Infisical credentials detected, fetching secrets..."
 8: 
 9: 
10:     [ -n "$INFISICAL_SITE_URL" ] && export INFISICAL_API_URL="$INFISICAL_SITE_URL"
11: 
12: 
13:     export INFISICAL_TOKEN=$(infisical login \
14:         --method=universal-auth \
15:         --client-id="$INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID" \
16:         --client-secret="$INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET" \
17:         --silent --plain)
18: 
19: 
20:     echo "Loading /postgresql secrets..."
21:     eval "$(infisical export --env="$INFISICAL_ENV" --projectId="$INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID" --path="/postgresql" --format=dotenv-export)"
22: 
23:     echo "Loading /keycloak secrets..."
24:     eval "$(infisical export --env="$INFISICAL_ENV" --projectId="$INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID" --path="/keycloak" --format=dotenv-export)"
25: 
26:     echo "Loading /api secrets..."
27:     eval "$(infisical export --env="$INFISICAL_ENV" --projectId="$INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID" --path="/api" --format=dotenv-export)"
28: 
29:     echo "All secrets loaded successfully."
30: else
31:     echo "No Infisical credentials found, using existing environment variables."
32: fi
33: 
34: echo "Starting .NET application..."
35: exec dotnet Explore.API.dll "$@"
````

55:     public void OnAuthorization(AuthorizationFilterContext context)
56:     {
57:         var deploymentSettings = context.HttpContext.RequestServices
58:             .GetRequiredService<IOptions<DeploymentSettings>>().Value;
59: 
60:         if (deploymentSettings.IsSingleTenant)
61:         {
62:             context.Result = new ObjectResult(new
63:             {
64:                 error = "MultiTenantRequired",
65:                 message = "This endpoint is only available in multi-tenant deployments."
66:             })
67:             {
68:                 StatusCode = StatusCodes.Status403Forbidden
69:             };
70:         }
71:     }
72: }
````
